anchors.description: Overall frame width of the double-leaf glass entrance door of house 64, between the outer top corners of its white frame.
anchors.visible_evidence: Both glass leaves, the central meeting stile and both outer jambs of the double door are fully visible; both points sit on the outer top corners of the door frame.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Leaves may be 0.90 m or 1.00 m wide, so the outer width is about 1.8-2.1 m; the facade is viewed obliquely, so only the 3D distance between the frame corners is used.

anchors.description: Height of the glass entrance door from the top frame edge down to the threshold at the floor, measured across the left leaf.
anchors.visible_evidence: The door top frame and the bottom rail with the threshold line are visible; the pair lies on the top and bottom edges of the left door leaf.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Modern entrance doors are 2.1-2.4 m high; the exact leaf height including frame is not directly readable, so the interval covers that range.

anchors.description: Height of the single-leaf grey steel door (technical side entrance) next to the scaffolding, from the top frame edge to the door sill.
anchors.visible_evidence: The grey steel door and its frame are visible between the white utility box and the scaffold pole; the top frame line and the bottom rail/sill line are both visible at this column.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: A standard 0.9 x 2.0-2.1 m single-leaf door; the bottom edge is close to a small sill/ramp so the base line is uncertain by about 5 cm.
